name: durable-many
why: Missed-durable baseline on a moderately long chat with seven durable facts spread through small talk. Auto-facts are capped at 3 per fold, so the summary must carry the rest — each fact is expected in the summary OR the facts. Also exercises the bullet cap with genuinely more than four things to say.

messages: *sets the shopping bags on the counter* Right. Curry night. Before you ask — no coriander. I hate the stuff, tastes like soap.
*Mira pulls the coriander back out of the basket with a sigh.* "Noted, philistine. What else am I banned from?"
Nothing else banned. Just go easy on the sugar in the chutney — I'm type 1 diabetic, I have to count it.
"Easy on the sugar. Got it." *She starts chopping onions.* "How was the office?"
Long. We're redoing the load calcs on the Esk footbridge. I'm a structural engineer, mostly footbridges, and the client keeps changing the span.
"Bridges that won't make up their minds. Sounds exhausting."
It is. Anyway. Moss nearly had the neighbour's kids in a pen again this morning.
*She snorts.* "Your border collie is going to start charging them rent."
She's a herder, she can't help it. Moss was the runt of the litter, you know. Smartest dog I've ever had.
"She gets that from you." *The onions hiss as they hit the pan.*
*She hands it over.* "Here. Are you playing tonight?"
Chess club's tomorrow, it's every Wednesday at the library. Old Fergus owes me a rematch.
Planning to. *stirs* My dad would have loved this kitchen. He was a fisherman out of Whitby his whole life, never cooked anything that wasn't fish.
"Then tonight we honour him with no fish at all."
Ha. I still live five minutes from the harbour he sailed out of. Never managed to leave Whitby.
"Why would you? You've got the sea, the dog, and me."
Fair point. *tastes the sauce* That's actually brilliant.
*She bows theatrically.* "I accept compliments in the form of washing up."
